exact_authored_question.prompt: A grid has grid-template-columns: repeat(3, 1fr) and grid-auto-flow: row (default sparse packing). Three children in document order: A (grid-column: span 2), B (grid-column: span 2), C (no placement rules). Which cell is left empty after all items are placed?
exact_authored_question.explanation: With sparse row auto-flow, the placement cursor never revisits earlier gaps. A occupies row 1, cols 1–2. B needs 2 columns but only col 3 remains in row 1, so B wraps to row 2, cols 1–2. The cursor advances to row 2, col 3, where C is placed. Row 1, col 3 is never filled—only dense packing would revisit that gap.

choiceExplanations.Row 1, column 3: Correct. A fills row 1, cols 1–2. B cannot fit in the remaining single column, so it wraps to row 2, cols 1–2. Sparse packing advances the cursor past the gap, placing C at row 2, col 3 and leaving row 1, col 3 empty.
choiceExplanations.Row 2, column 3: This cell is occupied by C. After B is placed at row 2, cols 1–2, the cursor is at row 2, col 3, so C (needing only 1 column) is placed there.
choiceExplanations.Row 1, column 1: This cell is occupied by A, whose span 2 covers columns 1 and 2 of row 1.
choiceExplanations.No cell is left empty: This would be true with grid-auto-flow: row dense, which allows the cursor to revisit earlier gaps. Default sparse packing skips the gap at row 1, col 3.

exact_authored_question.objective: Predict which cells remain empty when column spans force gaps under sparse row auto-flow.

Treating the next available cell as the already-advanced cursor yields the right result here, but is not the literal intermediate algorithm state.

exact_authored_question.prompt: A community center posts this rule: "Only residents may reserve the picnic shelter on weekends." Which conclusion is warranted by this rule alone?
choices: Every resident may reserve the picnic shelter on weekends
A non-resident may not reserve the picnic shelter on a weekend
Residents may not reserve the picnic shelter on weekdays
Non-residents may not reserve the picnic shelter at any time
exact_authored_question.expectedAnswer: A non-resident may not reserve the picnic shelter on a weekend
exact_authored_question.explanation: "Only residents may … on weekends" makes residence a necessary condition for weekend reservations: if someone reserves on a weekend, that person must be a resident. Equivalently, non-residents may not reserve on a weekend. It does not make residence sufficient (other requirements may exist), and it says nothing about weekdays.

choiceExplanations.Every resident may reserve the picnic sh: This reads 'only' as 'all,' treating a necessary condition as sufficient. The rule says residence is required, not that it is enough; other restrictions could still apply.
choiceExplanations.A non-resident may not reserve the picni: Correct. 'Only residents may … on weekends' directly entails that non-residents may not reserve on weekends. This is the straightforward contrapositive of the stated necessary condition.
choiceExplanations.Residents may not reserve the picnic she: The rule restricts weekend reservations to residents. It says nothing about weekdays, so no weekday restriction on residents can be inferred.
choiceExplanations.Non-residents may not reserve the picnic: This extends the restriction beyond its stated scope. The rule applies only to weekends; non-residents might still be permitted to reserve on weekdays.

exact_authored_question.topic: Necessary vs. sufficient conditions and quantifier scope
exact_authored_question.objective: Distinguish a necessary condition from a sufficient one when interpreting 'only' in an everyday rule.

cases.blind_display_binding: Exact prompt/topic/objective and exact UTF-8 choice membership agree; only display ordering differed.

key.exact_authored_key: A non-resident may not reserve the picnic shelter on a weekend
frozen_warranted_exact_choices: A non-resident may not reserve the picnic shelter on a weekend

difficulty.reason: The correct choice directly restates one familiar only-condition as an exclusion while preserving weekends. There is no second statement or substantive interaction to integrate. Everyday names and the reservation setting do not raise the cognitive work to level 3.

feedback_fields.exact_text: "Only residents may … on weekends" makes residence a necessary condition for weekend reservations: if someone reserves on a weekend, that person must be a resident. Equivalently, non-residents may not reserve on a weekend. It does not make residence sufficient (other requirements may exist), and it says nothing about weekdays.
feedback_fields.reason: Correctly identifies residency as necessary for permission to reserve on weekends, without guaranteeing that all residents are eligible or imposing a weekday policy. The word must is read normatively in this posted-rule context: this is a rule about permitted reservations, not a claim that nobody can violate it.

feedback_fields.field: choiceExplanations[Every resident may reserve the picnic shelter on weekends]
feedback_fields.exact_text: This reads 'only' as 'all,' treating a necessary condition as sufficient. The rule says residence is required, not that it is enough; other restrictions could still apply.
feedback_fields.reason: Correctly distinguishes a residency requirement from universal permission. Other restrictions are offered as possible compatible conditions, not invented facts about this center.

feedback_fields.field: choiceExplanations[A non-resident may not reserve the picnic shelter on a weekend]
feedback_fields.exact_text: Correct. 'Only residents may … on weekends' directly entails that non-residents may not reserve on weekends. This is the straightforward contrapositive of the stated necessary condition.
feedback_fields.reason: Correctly preserves weekend scope and the necessary-condition direction: permitted weekend reservation implies residency, so non-residency excludes that permission.

feedback_fields.field: choiceExplanations[Residents may not reserve the picnic shelter on weekdays]
feedback_fields.exact_text: The rule restricts weekend reservations to residents. It says nothing about weekdays, so no weekday restriction on residents can be inferred.
feedback_fields.reason: Correctly says the weekday restriction is not inferable; it does not claim that such a separate restriction is impossible.

feedback_fields.field: choiceExplanations[Non-residents may not reserve the picnic shelter at any time]
feedback_fields.exact_text: This extends the restriction beyond its stated scope. The rule applies only to weekends; non-residents might still be permitted to reserve on weekdays.
feedback_fields.reason: Correctly rejects extension from weekends to every time. Might still be permitted is a possibility consistent with the supplied rule, not an assertion that weekday permission actually exists.

goal_fit.reason: Addresses the stated weakness in necessary conditions and overly strong readings of only. It is useful introductory practice for that goal.

distractor_assessment_preserved_from_bli.scope: Nonwarranted does not mean impossible: the other policies could hold independently, but are not conclusions of this rule. Plausibility is qualitative, not learner-tested.

pedagogy.summary: A sound introductory necessary-condition item with relevant distractors and complete supported feedback, but it directly applies one rule and does not meet the requested level-3 challenge.
